main_text.p: mò, ferendo testimonium hoc à nobis factum esse vel non factum esse: quales sunt istæ Rhetorum formulæ, in quaestione Facti, Occidistine matrem, Orcstes? Conscientia respondet, Occidi. Secundò, ferendo judicium, quod factum est vel omissum, bene sit an male factum, rectène sit an perperam omissum; ut in quaestione Juris apud Rhetores, ubi de facto constat Occidistine Clodium Milo? Occidi. Fateris ergo te sontem? Jure occidi. In Prima applicatione procedit Conscientia per modum Testis: in Secunda, per modum Judicis. Officia autem & actus ejus sunt, in primo processu testimonium perhibere: in secundo processu arguere, accusare, excusare, defendere, condemnare, absolvere. Unde oriuntur porro in anima varii effectus: à redarguente, accusante, condemnante conscientia summa animi tristitia & inquietudo, remorsus, terrores, tormenta; è contra ab excusante, defendente & absolvente, summa animi lætitia & tranquillitas, gaudium & solatium ineffabile, quies[?] arrecta, fiducia intrepida, & inconcussa mentis constantia. Tertiæ Conscientiæ applicatio respicit futura facienda; in qua procedit Conscientia per modum Legislatoris, Præceptoris, Monitoris, aut Conciliarii. Et in isto processu, ejus actus & officia sunt dictare, obligare, instigare, retrahere. Hi sunt præcipui Conscientiæ Actus: cujus vocem recta monentis qui audierit, nec Testem ipsam multum reformidabit, nec Judicem.

XXVIII. Absolvi tandem, quæ de Conscientiæ Naturâ videbantur mihi dictu necessaria. Prolixius vereor, certè obscuriùs, quàm aut voluissem, aut debuissem, si res aliter tulisset[?]; aut quàm facturum me spero, in futuris (si Deus voluerit) de Conscientiæ usu Praelectionibus. page.notes: The left strip shows the edge of the facing page and is left out. The right-margin marks "2" and "3" are printed as bare numerals with no note text; they are placed at the lines where they stand. Doubtful readings: "quies[?]" (the word before "arrecta" is not clear); "tulisset[?]" (the form is partly obscured). "Praelectionibus" and "Præleƈtio" in the running head use the printed ligature spelling as far as it could be read. Catchword "teriæ" is printed at the right below the last line and is the start of the next page's word "materiæ".
